body: EU AI Act Article 50(2) requires providers of AI systems that generate synthetic audio, image, video, or text content to mark the output in a machine-readable format and label it as artificially generated or manipulated. The obligation is effective from August 2026; it is a technical marking duty, not optional disclosure. For the Council of AI, machine-readable marking is the bridge between monitored containment and verified measurement: an observed boundary is only auditable when the synthetic origin of each output is machine-readable and links back to the manifest and timestamp under which it was produced. The verified measurement credential includes, where the system produces synthetic media, the machine-readable marking metadata as part of the signed observation — so an auditor can confirm both the score and the provenance of the content being scored. Monitored containment (measurement of boundary behavior) is not provable isolation (an unattainable claim of perfect separation). The Council Signal containment index records marking-related observations alongside other axis measurements; the manifest binds them together.
